title: Context and memory in the makerspace assistant

items.stem: Your program calls the model three times to finish one student request. On the third call, how does the model know what happened in the first call?

options.text: It stored the first call itself, so nothing needs to be sent again
Your program sends the earlier history again as part of the input
It learned from the first call and adjusted itself before the next
The tool that ran in between keeps the history and tells the model

items.stem: In your assistant, instructions and tool descriptions take 1,000 tokens, and the student's message is 20 tokens. Call 1: the model replies with a tool request of 30 tokens. The tool result is 200 tokens. Call 2: the model writes its final answer of 50 tokens. Each call's input is everything in the window so far. How many input tokens do the two calls use in total?
Yesterday a student told the assistant which machines they train on. Today, in a new chat, the assistant has no idea. In one sentence, what is missing from the design?
The 30-page soldering guide is about 12,000 tokens. It is the same for every student, and about one question in ten needs it. Where should it live in the assistant?

options.text: In the window on every call, so the model always has it ready
In each student's note file, so it is loaded at every visit
In the instructions, repeated once for each step of the loop
In a searchable store, with a few passages fetched per question

items.stem: A student asks about the vinyl cutter, but no vinyl cutter manual is in your search store. The search still returns its 3 closest chunks, all about other machines. What should the assistant do?

options.text: Answer from the closest chunks, since search always finds the page
Say the manuals don't cover it, because the chunks don't answer it
Retrain the model on the manuals so that it can answer next time
Save the question as a note and reply with the first chunk's text
